events.title: Adolphe Sax, Inventor of the Saxophone, Is Born
events.description: Belgian instrument maker Adolphe Sax was born on this day in Dinant. He went on to patent the saxophone in the 1840s, an instrument that blends the power of brass with the agility of woodwinds.
events.significance: The saxophone became central to jazz, blues, classical and popular music, and it shaped the sound of the 20th century.

events.title: John Philip Sousa, the 'March King,' Is Born
events.description: American composer and bandleader John Philip Sousa was born on November 6, 1854. He wrote marches including 'The Stars and Stripes Forever' and led the U.S. Marine Band.
events.significance: Sousa's stirring marches became a lasting part of American patriotic music. 'The Stars and Stripes Forever' is the official national march of the United States.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln Is Elected President
events.description: Abraham Lincoln, a former Illinois congressman, won the U.S. presidential election and became the first Republican to hold the office. His victory came at a time of deep national division over slavery.
events.significance: Lincoln's election led Southern states to secede, and the Civil War followed. He led the Union through that war and set the country on the path to ending slavery.

events.title: Gandhi Is Arrested During the Indian Miners' March
events.description: Mohandas K. Gandhi led a large group of Indian miners from Natal into the Transvaal in South Africa to protest discriminatory laws. Authorities arrested him on this day.
events.significance: The march was a landmark in Gandhi's development of nonviolent resistance. He later used the same approach in India's independence movement.
